subject: Urgent: Third-party infringement notice — indemnity & evidence needed
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@orchidtech.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@orchidtech.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Third-party infringement notice — Redwood usage in flagged model

Hi Priyom,

We received a third-party claim this morning alleging that outputs delivered via Redwood-hosted model instances contain material that may infringe a third party's IP. I attached the claimant's notice (Orchid_Tech_Claim_Notice.pdf) for your review.

Two asks to start: can Redwood confirm whether the customer order form / MSA and your indemnity provisions would apply if this claim proceeds to notice? Second, can you provide a point of contact for evidence (logs, K-V cache slices, request IDs) so we can assess scope quickly — our procurement team needs this for review.

We're under a 10-business-day review window from the claimant and procurement is escalating this for contract clarity. Can you confirm by EOD?

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Legal Ops | OrchidTech

Attachment: Orchid_Tech_Claim_Notice.pdf (PDF, 280 KB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@orchidtech.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Third-party infringement notice — Redwood usage in flagged model

Sarah — thanks for sending, and sorry you're dealing with this. We can support a review but need to coordinate legal + engineering evidence capture. High-level: OrchidTech's Order Form (ORC-4821) references our standard MSA, which contains the customer indemnity clause and the usual defend-or-reimburse framework. There are a few order-form-specific carveouts we should confirm with you (e.g., model fine-tune scope, hosted vs. private deployment).

Immediate actions from our side:
- I copied Kimberly (counsel) for contract position and Ben (CS) for evidence capture/IDS.
- Ben, can you pull the request IDs, KV cache snapshots, and any stored input artifacts for the timeframe Sarah notes? Prefer CSV manifest and a short readme (who/when) — we can put these on a shared Drive link.
- Kimberly, quick read: are we likely to take defense control here or propose a limited cooperation plus insurance-offset approach?

Sarah — I'll confirm a working plan by EOD and we should schedule a 30-minute triage call tomorrow so procurement and legal can align.

Best,
Priyom
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Attachment: (none)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Third-party infringement notice — Redwood usage in flagged model

Priyom / team — quick contract/legal note for the triage:

1) Defense vs. Reimburse: Our MSA's baseline is "defend or reimburse" for third-party IP claims arising from customer use of the Service, subject to the exclusions in Section 7.2. However, order-forms frequently add carveouts for model-generated output or data-subset limitations. If Orchid's order form contains any "AI-output" carveout or narrow indemnity cap, that will change negotiation posture.

2) Recommended short-term position to communicate to Orchid: we are prepared to cooperate and provide evidence (logs + request IDs) and, per the MSA, we will evaluate the claim and either (a) assume defense with Redwood counsel where the claim squarely arises from our infrastructure/service defects, or (b) reimburse reasonable settlement costs where the claim is tied to customer-provided content or fine-tuning data. We should avoid an unconditional acceptance of defense control at this stage.

3) Evidence ask (what Legal needs from Engineering/CS):
- precise request IDs: list of UUIDs and timestamps
- model variant and exact model SHA or published variant name
- sequence length and prompt text redaction guidance (we should not share full PII)
- minimal KV cache slices that map to the allegations (timeboxed)
- any opt-in fine-tune dataset manifests (if customer fine-tuned)

4) Insurance and offsets: propose we ask Orchid to confirm their insurance layer and whether they expect insurance to be primary. We can offer an insurance-offset mechanism (Redwood's liability limited to policy + cap in MSA) as a negotiation avenue.

I'll draft suggested language for a limited acceptance of defense with cooperation conditions and ask Sales to run that by the customer.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_sec7_redline_excerpt.txt (text, 4 KB)

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@orchidtech.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@orchidtech.com
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Third-party infringement notice — Redwood usage in flagged model

Thanks, Priyom / Kimberly. A couple quick clarifications from Orchid:

- Our Order Form includes the standard indemnity reference but no explicit "AI-output" carveout; Orchid considered but did not include that language in v3.
- Procurement wants explicit commitment that Redwood will "defend" rather than limit to reimbursement — our legal has flagged commercial risk if defense control is refused.
- We've uploaded the claimant's exhibit package to the Drive link in my original email and added the PoC (screenshots + sample prompts).

For timing: procurement needs Redwood's proposed redline language and evidence manifest by EOD tomorrow to avoid pausing the deal. We can do a triage call at 11:00 AM PT if that works.

Sarah Liu
Legal Ops | OrchidTech

Attachment: claimant_exhibits.zip (ZIP, 1.2 MB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@orchidtech.com>, procure@orchidtech.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Third-party infringement notice — Redwood usage in flagged model

Team — quick update and proposed next steps before the 11:00 AM PT triage: 

1) Evidence: Ben will deliver a CSV manifest and a redacted request bundle to the Drive link by 07:30 AM PT tomorrow (15 May). Ben — please include the model variant, request IDs, timestamps, and a short readme linking to the exhibit files.

2) Contract posture (Kimberly's suggested compromise): propose language that offers defense "subject to Redwood's right to control defense when the claim arises from Redwood's infrastructure or service delivery; where the claim arises from customer data or prompts, Redwood will cooperate and reimburse reasonable settlement and defense costs proportionate to Redwood's responsibility." This preserves our defend-or-reimburse framework but avoids unconditional, unlimited defense control.

3) Canary fallback plan: if Orchid cannot accept the compromise by EOD, we will offer a narrowly scoped, time-limited warranty: Redwood will accept defense for the specific claim window (the dates in the claimant's exhibit) while both parties preserve their positions for other claims; this is intended to keep the deal moving while we complete joint fact-finding.

4) Ask of Orchid: please confirm insurance contact and whether they expect defense costs to be fronted by their carrier. Also confirm procurement will accept the triage call at 11:00 AM PT.

I'll circulate Kimberly's draft redline before the call. Thanks all — want to keep the deal momentum while protecting Redwood exposure.

Priyom Das
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Attachment: (will circulate Kimberly's redline snippet before call)
